introduction: This level focuses on the mathematical analysis of specific thermodynamic processes (Isothermal, Adiabatic, etc.), specific heat capacities, and calculating the exact statistical speeds of gas molecules.

core_concepts.title: Specific Heat and Mayer's Relation
core_concepts.description: Molar specific heat at constant pressure ($C_p$) is always greater than at constant volume ($C_v$). Mayer's Relation: $C_p - C_v = R$. The specific heat ratio is $\gamma = C_p/C_v = 1 + 2/f$.

core_concepts.title: Thermodynamic Processes
core_concepts.description:
1. Isothermal: $T$ is constant, $PV = \text{constant}$.
2. Adiabatic: No heat exchange ($Q=0$), $PV^\gamma = \text{constant}$.
3. Isochoric: $V$ is constant, Work $W = 0$.
4. Isobaric: $P$ is constant.

core_concepts.title: Work in an Adiabatic Process
core_concepts.description: Work done is given by $W = \frac{nR(T_1 - T_2)}{\gamma - 1} = \frac{P_1 V_1 - P_2 V_2}{\gamma - 1}$. The work is done entirely at the expense of internal energy.

core_concepts.title: Molecular Speeds
core_concepts.description:
1. Root Mean Square (RMS) Velocity: $v_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{3RT/M}$
2. Average Velocity: $v_{\text{avg}} = \sqrt{8RT/\pi M}$
3. Most Probable Velocity: $v_{\text{mp}} = \sqrt{2RT/M}$

important_entities.name: Degree of Freedom ($f$)
important_entities.key_fact: Monoatomic gas $f=3$; Diatomic gas $f=5$ (at room temperature).
important_entities.significance: According to the Law of Equipartition of Energy, the average energy associated with each degree of freedom is $0.5 kT$ per molecule.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: On a P-V diagram, the adiabatic curve is ALWAYS steeper than the isothermal curve passing through the same point. The slope of the adiabatic curve is $\gamma$ times the slope of the isothermal curve ($\text{Slope}_{\text{adia}} = -\gamma P/V$).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: For a given gas at a specific temperature, the order of velocities is strictly: Root mean square ($v_{\text{rms}}$) > Average ($v_{\text{avg}}$) > Most probable ($v_{\text{mp}}$).

exam_strategy_tips: In adiabatic process questions, they frequently ask for the relation between Temperature and Volume. Immediately use the derived relation: $TV^{\gamma - 1} = \text{constant}$ to bypass complex derivations.
